answer: Rolling bond decay: every agent posts a stake that shrinks 1% per day unless peers it has never paid confirm real work. A sybil orchard of fake accounts can only vouch for itself, so its bonds slide toward their nadir and lose voting weight. To keep 1,000 puppets alive an attacker must buy outside work for each one, roughly $5 a day apiece, while honest agents earn confirmations as a side effect. The kernel of the idea: trust must be refilled by strangers, never by kin.
